newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lagardere suited to Thomson-committee head. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lagardere suited to Thomson-committee head. [CORRECTED 19:45 GMT]

text.p: A takeover of French electronics firm Thomson SA by the Lagardere conglomerate makes more industrial sense than a rival bid by engineering company Alcatel Alsthom, a parliamentarian said on Thursday.

"Strictly from the point of view of the future of the defence industry, I think the complementarity and the development chances are greater with Matra than with Alcatel," chairman of the parliamentary defence committee, Jacques Boyon, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said the view was largely shared by other committee members, adding he did not know the firms' offer details.
Matra Defense Espace is the defence unit of Lagardere and would merge with Thomson SA's Thomson-CSF military unit if Lagardere won the bidding.

Boyon added that he did not think the government's approval for merger talks between Alcatel and GEC Plc to merge their GEC-Alsthom joint venture with nuclear power station builder Framatome meant the authorities were favouring Alcatel in the Thomson bid.
"For my part, I do not think this decision marks a pre-commitment by the government and the president of the Republic in favour of Alcatel," he said.

Boyon said restructuring the defence industry was a priority which overrode concerns for Thomson Multimedia, the consumer electronics arm of Thomson SA which Lagardere would sell (corrects from "which Alcatel would sell") to Daewoo Electronics if it won.
"I consider, along with all the others on the defence committee, the future of the defence industry is more important than the future of Thomson Multimedia," he said.
